messages.author: b5f242e7eb90c7c9
messages.subject: simulateData and skewness and kurtosis
parts:
Dear all,

I have been trying to simulate the skewness and kurtosis of observed variables. If I understand in one of the previous posts here correctly, simulating skewness and kurtosis using Vale–Maurelli approach (the method that simulateData is using) can lead to inaccurate skewness and kurtosis values. Below are my simulation results and I found the same problem in my simulation results. I wonder if there is any workaround for this?

Thank you!

Chester

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

model.2015 <- "
f1 =~ 0.6*v10+0.6*v11+0.6*v12+0.6*v13+0.6*v14+0.6*v15+0.6*v16+0.6*v17+0.6*v18+0.6*v19
f2 =~ 0.6*v20+0.6*v21+0.6*v22+0.6*v23+0.6*v24+0.6*v25+0.6*v26+0.6*v27+0.6*v28+0.6*v29

f1 ~~ (-0.4)*f2

v10 ~ 3*1
v11 ~ 3*1
v12 ~ 3*1
v13 ~ 3*1
v14 ~ 3*1
v15 ~ 3*1
v16 ~ 3*1
v17 ~ 3*1
v18 ~ 3*1
v19 ~ 3*1

v20 ~ 3*1
v21 ~ 3*1
v22 ~ 3*1
v23 ~ 3*1
v24 ~ 3*1
v25 ~ 3*1
v26 ~ 3*1
v27 ~ 3*1
v28 ~ 3*1
v29 ~ 3*1
"

data.2015 <- simulateData(model = model.2015, model.type = "cfa", sample.nobs = 100000L, standardized = TRUE, seed = 123,
                          skewness = c(rep(5,10),rep(5,10)), kurtosis = c(rep(6,10),rep(6,10)))

> mean(data.2015$v10)
[1] 3.001978
> mean(data.2015$v20)
[1] 3.001728
> moments::skewness(data.2015$v10)
[1] 1.849688
> moments::skewness(data.2015$v20)
[1] 1.865931
> moments::kurtosis(data.2015$v10)
[1] 7.127018
> moments::kurtosis(data.2015$v20)
[1] 7.300465
